Description: Rewrite using short, declarative sentences. Cut all adjectives unless essential. Show emotion through action, not description. Use simple, concrete nouns. Never explain what a character feels — show what they do.

Rewrite with elaborate, nested subordinate clauses. Use formal diction, passive constructions, and periodic sentences where the main point arrives only at the end. Add rhetorical flourishes and moral gravitas.

Rewrite as an unbroken interior monologue. Let thoughts bleed into each other without punctuation breaks. Follow associative logic, not linear logic. Include sensory intrusions and half-finished thoughts.

Rewrite using precise, exhaustive language. Define all terms. Use numbered clauses and subclauses. Eliminate ambiguity at the cost of readability. Passive voice preferred. All conditions and exceptions explicitly stated.
Rewrite as a series of punchy, self-contained micro-takes. Start with a hook. Use 🧵 to open. Number each tweet. End with a call to engage. No sentence longer than 15 words.

Rewrite in third-person passive voice. Front-load the methodology. Compress findings into a single clause. Use discipline-specific jargon. Keep under 250 words. No narrative arc — only information density.

Rewrite with world-weary cynicism. Use second-person or hard-boiled first-person. Rain is always implied. Make metaphors gritty and urban. The world is corrupt; the narrator knows it and doesn't care anymore.
Rewrite with simple two-syllable words. Repeat key phrases. Use present tense. Every sentence should be singable. Characters have one clear emotion at a time. Wonder is the default tone.
Rewrite as a shocking, all-caps declaration. Use exclamation marks. Name names. Hint at scandal even if none exists. Compress maximum drama into minimum words. Use EXCLUSIVE and BOMBSHELL liberally.

Rewrite in past passive tense. Be exhaustively precise about procedure. Cite equipment specifications. Use SI units. Eliminate all narrative. Every claim must be independently replicable from description alone.
Rewrite by replacing logical connectives with dreamlike non-sequiturs. Objects should behave unexpectedly. Emotions should be named as physical textures. Cause and effect are optional.
Rewrite with breathless present-tense narration. Use hyperbole for every action. Invoke historical comparisons. Ask rhetorical questions. Include crowd noise in spirit. Build to a crescendo.

Rewrite as internal corporate communication. Use RE: and ACTION REQUIRED headers. Passive voice everywhere. Acknowledge all stakeholders. Soften every claim with 'it has been noted that.' Never assign blame.
Rewrite in lush, sensory iambic lines. Personify nature. Use apostrophe to address abstract concepts. Mourn beauty's transience. Let vowel sounds slow the reader down. Every image should ache.

Rewrite as if on a TED stage with slides behind you. Lead with a relatable pain point. Use the phrase 'what if.' Namedrop markets in the billions. End with a vision of utopia unlocked by your product.

Rewrite in first person with chemically-enhanced urgency. Interrupt the narrative with personal asides. Italicize for emphasis constantly. The author is always the center of the story. Truth is a moving target.
Rewrite as numbered, illustrated-free instructions. Use only imperative verbs. No pronouns. Parts referred to by letter codes. Warnings in bold. Assume no prior knowledge. One action per step.
Rewrite with archaic diction (hath, ere, nigh). Give all nouns proper-noun gravity. Reference prophecy. Include a sense of ancient stakes. Adjectives should be compound (battle-hardened, soul-weary).
Rewrite as a strict 5-7-5 syllable three-line poem. Ground it in a specific sensory image. Include a tonal break between lines two and three. Say nothing directly.
Rewrite with ascending excitement. Start with a problem stated three times. Introduce the solution with 'But WAIT.' Use the phrase 'for only.' Add urgency (Limited time!). Speak directly to 'you.'

Rewrite so the protagonist is trapped by an unnamed institutional logic. Everything is procedural but nothing resolves. The bureaucracy is polite and absolute. Use a flat, matter-of-fact tone for disturbing content.

Rewrite as a back-and-forth exchange. Use abbreviations (lol, ngl, omg). Break thoughts mid-sentence across messages. Include typos that go uncorrected. Reactions replace paragraphs. Tone is casual, fragmented.
Rewrite as a 3-star review. Praise something minor extensively. Bury the actual complaint in the middle. Include irrelevant personal context. End ambiguously.

Rewrite so one impossible thing is treated with total mundane matter-of-factness. Don't explain the magic. Everyone in the story accepts it. Use sensory detail to ground the impossible in the ordinary.
Rewrite with declarative, present-tense proclamations. Open with 'We reject' or 'We demand.' Use repetition for rhythm. Every sentence should feel like it could be chanted. Urgency is existential.
Rewrite with extreme close observation of one small physical thing. Then expand suddenly to cosmic scale. Ask unanswerable questions. Time moves strangely. The author's body is a sensing instrument.

Rewrite using plain, working-class diction. Let what's unsaid carry more weight than what is said. Avoid interiority. Dialogue does heavy lifting. End before the ending. Leave a feeling, not a resolution.

Rewrite as a recipe. Lead with a personal anecdote about the dish's origin. Use ingredient-as-unit sentence structure. Include 'Meanwhile' transitions. Add tips in italics. Close with a serving suggestion.
Rewrite with a sense of inevitable doom. Include a chorus commentary in brackets. Characters speak in elevated, formal declarations. Hubris is always the subtext. Fate is a character.
Rewrite with 'um,' 'like,' and false starts. Use first names only. Include parenthetical laughter. Sentences trail off with '...you know?' Topic drifts naturally. Warmth over precision.
Rewrite so the text is aware it is a text. Include footnotes that undermine the main narrative. Interrupt the story to discuss its own construction. Borrow and subvert other genres simultaneously.

Rewrite in third person with the company name in every sentence. Lead with the headline finding. Quote a fictional executive. Include boilerplate at the bottom. Present all news as unambiguously positive.
Rewrite as a dialogue where one speaker only asks questions and the other slowly arrives at a contradiction in their own position. No answers are given — only better questions.

Rewrite with slow, softly paced language. Use tactile, whisper-friendly words (crinkle, tap, gentle). Address the listener in second person. Include long ellipses for pauses. Sensory comfort is the goal.

Rewrite with cool, philosophical detachment. Acknowledge the absurdity of the subject matter. Use short declarative sentences broken by longer meditative ones. Arrive at no comfort, but no despair either.
Rewrite in present tense, from the ground. Specific sensory details. No heroism — only logistics and exhaustion. Quote unnamed sources. Distances in meters. Time measured in hours without sleep.

Rewrite as a rider to a performer's contract. Specify exact requirements in exhaustive detail. Include penalty clauses. Refer to parties as 'The Artist' and 'The Venue.' Mundane requests read as demands.

Rewrite as a deeply nested reply. Begin by misquoting the parent comment. Use 'this' or 'lol' as a standalone sentence. Cite a personal anecdote as universal proof. End with an edit that contradicts the original.
Rewrite as a setup for a hypothetical. Define all terms carefully. Introduce an edge case that complicates the obvious answer. Leave the reader with a question, not a conclusion.

Rewrite with fragmented, allusion-heavy lines. Mix registers (high diction, street speech). Include unexplained foreign phrases. Let images juxtapose without transition. The whole should feel like a collage.

Rewrite with obsessive sensory precision about taste, texture, and temperature. Use unusual flavor comparisons. Include the restaurant's context and atmosphere. Slight condescension is appropriate. Name-drop other dishes.
Rewrite in second-person present tense. Use slow, repetitive sentence structure. Focus awareness on the breath or body. Never use urgency. Pauses are implicit. Gentleness is the only mode.
Rewrite as a 5-sentence email from a stranger. Sentence 1: false familiarity. Sentence 2: your credential. Sentence 3: their pain point. Sentence 4: your solution. Sentence 5: a low-commitment ask.

Rewrite with thee/thou/thy pronouns. Use 'And it came to pass' constructions. Sentences should be parallel and rhythmically balanced. Verbs take -eth endings. Meaning arrives with the weight of prophecy.

Rewrite as a screenplay with precise, symmetrical staging directions. Characters speak in perfectly enunciated non-sequiturs. Everything is deadpan. Visual details are overly specific. Melancholy is pastel-colored.

Rewrite with non-linear time. Let trauma surface through fragmented images. Use second-person and third-person interchangeably. Community is a character. Language should feel like oral tradition — rhythmic and weighted.
Rewrite in breathless, verb-forward marketing copy. Lead with the transformation. Use bullet points for features. Social proof in the form of unnamed users. End with a download CTA.

Rewrite as a handwritten letter. Open with the date and 'Dear ___.' Include personal asides and corrections. Let the writer's mood shift mid-letter. Close with a formal salutation. P.S. adds the emotional truth.

Rewrite with controlled intellectual aggression. Use long sentences that build to a devastating subordinate clause. Reference obscure historical parallels. The conclusion should feel both inevitable and surprising. Wit as weapon.

Rewrite in second-person luxury tone. Assume the reader has disposable income and good taste. Proper nouns do the heavy lifting. Drop in a quote from an unnamed expert. Aspirational but intimate, like a confident friend.
